raw_response.rationale: Full text read (18 pages). Although the study evaluates 647 rural handpump water points across eight councils in Cameroon's Mvila Division using the composite Water Service Sustainability Index (WSSI) alongside 103 semistructured water committee interviews, its quantitative component is strictly descriptive. It reports only weighted index percentages across councils (ranging from 26.57% in Mengong to 59.54% in Mvangan), descriptive indicator proportions (e.g., 32% nonfunctional, 67% unable to cover major repairs, 61% without active committees), and back-of-the-envelope arithmetic cost/savings approximations ($258,800 maintenance cost vs. $400,000 projected savings). No inferential statistical tests, regressions, correlation coefficients, standard errors, confidence intervals, or p-values are reported anywhere in the paper.
